advances: Continuous two-measure affine-line selection. It controls halfspaces containing the whole line and does not produce an actual mixed-integer point.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Fix $0<\alpha<\gamma_{r-1}$. For a unit vector $u$ let $E(u)=u^\perp$ and define
$$
F_i(u)=\{c\in E(u):\ \mu_i(\{x:b\cdot x\ge b\cdot c\})\ge\alpha
\text{ for all unit } b\in E(u)\}.
$$
The orthogonal marginal on $E(u)$ has a log-concave probability density by [Prékopa's marginal theorem](https://acta.bibl.u-szeged.hu/14411/1/math_034_335-343.pdf), Theorems 6 and 8 in an orthogonal coordinate system. It is full dimensional because the positive set of the original density contains an open ball. For $r-1\ge2$, its inverse power of exponent $-1/\beta$ is convex for $\beta>r$ by log-concavity, with the positive interior representative used by 7831e6cfc5f87556. That fact gives a projected point of depth at least $\gamma_{r-1}$. For $r=2$ the one-dimensional absolutely continuous marginal has a median with depth $1/2$. In either case this point has depth strictly above $\alpha$.

For fixed $i$, the map $(b,c)\mapsto\mu_i(\{x:b\cdot(x-c)\ge0\})$ is jointly continuous for unit $b$, since all limiting hyperplanes are null. Compactness of the unit sphere of $E(u)$ makes the strict gap uniform at the point just found, giving interior to $F_i(u)$ in $E(u)$. Each constraint defines a closed convex set by monotonicity in the threshold $b\cdot c$. For nonzero $c\in F_i(u)$, the choice $b=c/\|c\|$ gives $\mu_i(\{x:\|x\|\ge\|c\|\})\ge\alpha$, so all $F_i(u)$ are bounded uniformly in $u$. They are therefore nonempty compact convex sets. Their minimum-norm points $c_i(u)$ are unique and even in $u$.

To prove continuity, let $u_j\to u$ and let orthogonal maps $T_j\to I$ take $u$ to $u_j$, for example by small rotations. Every subsequential limit of $c_i(u_j)$ lies in $F_i(u)$ by testing each unit $b\in E(u)$ with $T_jb$ and taking the limit. Conversely, each relative interior point $c'$ of $F_i(u)$ has depth strictly above $\alpha$. Positive depth puts $c'$ in the interior of the closed support of the marginal by separation and nullity of hyperplanes. The marginal density has a positive lower bound in a small ball there by continuity of its finite logarithm on the positive interior. If some through-cap had mass exactly $\alpha$, moving $c'$ a small distance in its normal direction would stay in $F_i(u)$ but remove a slab of positive mass, a contradiction. By compactness of the unit normals the gap at $c'$ is uniform. Hence $T_jc'\in F_i(u_j)$ for large $j$: otherwise a subsequence of violating unit normals pulled back by $T_j^{-1}$ would converge to a unit normal in $E(u)$ contradicting the gap. Any point of $F_i(u)$ can be approximated by relative interior points on a segment to one interior point. Minimum-norm optimality against $T_jc'$ and passage to these limits give that every subsequential limit of $c_i(u_j)$ has norm at most the minimum norm in $F_i(u)$. Uniqueness and uniform boundedness now prove continuity.

The vector field $V(u)=c_1(u)-c_2(u)$ is even and orthogonal to $u$. If it were nowhere zero, $g(u)=V(u)/\|V(u)\|$ on $S^{r-1}$ would be homotopic to the identity via $\cos(\pi t/2)u+\sin(\pi t/2)g(u)$ for $0\le t\le1$. In particular $\deg g=1$. When $r-1$ is even, composing $g$ with the antipodal map leaves $g$ unchanged and multiplies its degree by $-1$. When $r-1$ is odd, the even map $g$ factors through the oriented double cover $S^{r-1}\to\mathbb{RP}^{r-1}$, so its degree is even. Both contradict degree one. Thus $c_1(u)=c_2(u)=c$ for some $u$, and $L_\alpha=c+\mathbb Ru$ has the required halfspace bound with $\alpha$. In fact, a proper halfspace containing the whole line has normal orthogonal to $u$ and contains its parallel halfspace with boundary through $c$.

Choose $\alpha_j\uparrow\gamma_{r-1}$ with $\alpha_1>0$, and write the resulting lines as $c_j+\mathbb Ru_j$ with $c_j\perp u_j$. The tail bound at $\alpha_1$ bounds all $c_j$. Pass to a subsequence with $(u_j,c_j)\to(u,c)$ and $c\perp u$. For any unit $b\in E(u)$, its normalized orthogonal projection onto $E(u_j)$ tends to $b$. The corresponding closed through-$c_j$ caps have mass at least $\alpha_j$ under each measure. Joint continuity gives mass at least $\gamma_{r-1}$ in the through-$c$ cap. By the parallel containment argument this proves the desired bound for all closed halfspaces containing $L=c+\mathbb Ru$. For a uniform compact convex body the projection of the body contains $c$, since otherwise separation gives a projected cap through $c$ of mass zero. Thus $L$ meets the body.
statement: Let $r\ge2$ and let $\mu_1,\mu_2$ be probability measures with full-dimensional log-concave Lebesgue densities on $\mathbb R^r$. There exists an affine line $L$ such that every closed halfspace containing $L$ has mass at least $\gamma_{r-1}=((r-1)/r)^{r-1}$ under each measure. If the measures are uniform on compact convex bodies, $L$ intersects both bodies.
title: Exact depth for a common line of two log-concave measures
